self_learning.lesson: A declared toolchain path can go stale in place, and a fail-closed gate will then report a MISSING binary rather than a MOVED one. Resolve the executable by glob and re-declare it in a ROUND-LOCAL copy; never edit the canonical declaration from inside a candidate round.

A lane probe that does not ASK the model for the nonce produces ERR_NO_ARM_EMITTED_NONCE even when the required arm served the turn with exit 0 and a valid usage receipt. The verdict token and the arm attribution are different questions.

`--guard-subject` must not cover the directory the dispatcher writes `--json-out` into, or the receipt's own write VOIDs the very verdict it records. Guard the artifacts; keep the receipt outside the guard.
self_learning.evidence: the VERIFY dispatch guards packet/ and the three receipt artifacts while writing its receipt to lane/

self_learning.lesson: A forbidden-path probe written as 'the path contains any of these substrings' is wrong: an evidence directory legitimately named product/ or credential/ inside the allowed prefix then reports a forbidden surface. The rule must be about WHERE the path resolves (outside the allowed prefix / outside EVIDENCE entirely) plus the git mode of changed paths.

A secret_assignment-style rule fires on `token = <expression>` in guard code that reasons ABOUT tokens, so it is a systematic false-positive class on security code. Store a MASKED enclosing line at scan time so each hit can be adjudicated by rule later without re-reading the blob and without ever reproducing a value.
Admission is not execution: a board can be created and look busy while nothing was ever claimed or completed. Read the board histogram back after driving it.
Truncating a CLI's stdout for a receipt BEFORE parsing it silently breaks the parse. Parse the full payload, trim only the stored copy.
